pages.text: Deep Seas also includes $(thing)Create High Seas$(): surface ships. They are the same kind of physical vessel as a $(l:ocean/submarines)submarine$(/l), but they float on top and travel by wind, engine or oar.

pages.title: Sail
pages.text: Comes in all 16 dyes. A ship needs enough canvas for its size, and big ships need more sails to get going.

pages.title: Wind Vane
pages.text: Shows wind direction. Steer along the arrow for top speed. Goggles show alignment as a percent.

Wind has a baseline, gusts, and extra strength in rain and thunderstorms. Terrain upwind can block it. Sailing straight into the wind keeps only part of your speed. A $(item)Rudder$() at the stern tells sails which way is forward; mount it on a Swivel Bearing to steer.

pages.title: Boat Engine
pages.text: A compact fuel-burning propeller. Mount it at the stern with the propeller in the water.

The engine burns fuel (open its fuel screen to see what it takes). Right-click to take the tiller, sneak to let go, sneak-click for the fuel screen. Hold use at the helm and move the mouse to set a speed limit from 0 to 15.

pages.title: Anchor
pages.text: Light in the air, one ton once it touches the bottom. Use a Steel Cable on it to connect a rope winch.

$(item)Oars$() give a stroke forward when used near water. A $(item)Buoy$() is a towable float you can ride and skip across the surface. Dyed $(item)Floaters$() from Deep Seas keep a plain boat on the surface.

pages.title: Seaglide
pages.text: Handheld twin fans for swimming. Runs on your hunger, not fuel. Break the surface at speed to leap out.

$(item)Steel Cables$() and $(item)Pulleys$() let a ship ride a cable. An $(item)Arresting Hook$() under a ship grabs a cable and brakes it, like a carrier landing. An $(item)Underwater Mine$() on a contraption detonates when entities or boats come close.
